doc.title: Al Chez interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, February 13, 2019

chapter: Getting and negotiating the Letterman job
title: The musicians union and Late Night horn subs
summary: Chez praises the AFM and recalls subbing on NBC's Late Night as horn player with Bruce Kapler, Ronnie Cuber and David Sanborn.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: And you’ve been in the musicians union for a long time. To do that show you probably had to be in the musicians union?

Yep. When I, yeah. The musicians union’s been great, AFM has been phenomenal. When I was out with Tower of Power — I did shows on like NBC when it was Late Night when it was at Rockefeller Center, before he moved to CBS. And me and Bruce Kapler, the saxophone player who was like a twenty year member of the CBS orchestra, me and him © Fillius Jazz Archive -12-
would be the horn players on Late Night whenever they needed horn players. We would bring in Ronnie Cuber, great baritone player, David Sanborn played alto.
They couldn’t find anybody good, yeah, yeah, yeah.
